title: Contextual Hub Switcher and Navigation Grid — Console IA Refresh
creator: Aisha Moreno
description: Redesign the Redwood Console information architecture and primary navigation to improve discoverability of dashboards, rollout controls, and cost views across multi-workspace customers. Replace current monolithic left rail with a contextual hub/grid that surfaces routes based on active workspace, user role, and recently used flows. Deliver prototypes for user testing and engineering handoff.
problem_statement: Engineers and product users report that key platform features (per-route cost breakdowns, rollout controls, and workspace-level dashboards) are buried in inconsistent locations. The current left rail mixes cross-workspace and workspace-scoped items and doesn't adapt to role or recent tasks, causing friction during incident triage and rollout configuration.
goals: Reduce time-to-find critical operational pages (dashboards, rollouts, cost breakdown) by 40% in task-based tests
Create a predictable workspace switcher pattern that preserves context and open routes when switching workspaces
Provide role-aware navigation so platform engineers see routing/infra controls while PMs see rollouts and cost summaries
Design a grid/hub landing that surfaces 6 contextual entry points with clear affordances for pinning and shortcuts
constraints: Left-rail width must stay within existing responsive breakpoints; avoid adding extra persistent chrome
Must integrate with existing RBAC/roles from backend APIs (no new auth model in this phase)
Prototype must map to existing route schema to keep migration effort bounded for Engineering
user_personas: Platform Engineer — needs fast access to model routing, capacity dashboards, and fallback policies
Product Manager — needs rollout status, canary results, and cost deltas for experiments
SRE/Oncall — needs immediate access to latency/error dashboards and workspace-scoped incidents
proposed_solutions: Contextual Hub Grid: replace static list with a top-level hub screen per workspace showing 6 tiles (Dashboards, Rollouts, Cost, Models, Routes, Activity). Each tile is a launchpad with secondary quick-actions.
Adaptive Left Rail: combine compact icon rail with an expandable contextual panel. Icons are global; expansion shows the hub grid or the last-open route within the current workspace.
Persistent Mini Switcher: workspace switcher becomes a persistent pill that preserves the open route; switching workspaces triggers an unobtrusive confirmation with 'Preserve context' option.
Role-aware Ordering: reorder tiles and quick actions based on role mutation returned from the auth API (PM/Eng/SRE).
chosen_solution: Hybrid: Adaptive Left Rail + Contextual Hub Grid. Keep the global compact icon rail for fast switching; when expanded the pane shows a hub grid that is populated by role and recent activity. Workspace switch preserves context by default and offers a 'reopen last route' toast when switching.
stakeholders: Engineering: Liam O'Connor (frontend lead), Chen Wei (runtime product engineer)
acceptance_criteria: Prototype validated with 12 cross-role participants; median task time to find 'Rollout details' decreases by >=40%
Engineering sign-off on route mapping and left-rail integration approach
Design tokens and CSS variables documented for the hub to ensure parity across Console themes
Accessibility audit pass for keyboard focus, ARIA labels, and color contrast
usability_findings: Initial 6-participant study showed confusion around icon-only compact rail — added hover labels and an expand affordance. Participants liked the hub tiles for bundling related actions but wanted quicker access to a pinned 'Cost Summary' for enterprise billing triage.
accessibility_notes: Ensure hub tiles use button semantics, maintain 4.5:1 contrast for body copy and 3:1 for large tile titles, provide skip-to-hub link for keyboard-only users, and surface aria-current on active routes.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): expose hub grid behind feature flag to 10% of orgs and internal testing workspaces. Monitor navigation time and error rates via Console telemetry. Phase 2: add role-aware ordering and pinning. Phase 3: full rollout with migration script to preserve user pins and last-open routes.
risks: Users who rely on muscle-memory for left-rail may be temporarily slowed — mitigate via gradual rollout and in-app tour
Complexity in preserving route state across legacy deep-links — engineering to provide mapping layer
Performance impact on initial hub population for orgs with many workspaces — lazy-load hub tiles
engineering_notes: Frontend will implement adaptive rail as a shallow component wrapper. Backend needs to expose recentRoutes(workspaceId) and rolePriority(userId) endpoints. Migration utility should be idempotent and run in the background.
open_questions: Should pinned tiles be global across the account or scoped per workspace?
How do we handle third-party integrations that add custom console routes?
What is the desired fallback when role metadata is unavailable?
